newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Maranda jumps on Zambian copper project win.
newsitem.headline: Maranda jumps on Zambian copper project win.

text.p: Shares in South African mining firm Maranda Mining Co Ltd jumped over six percent to a new year high on Friday on news the firm was part of a consortium which had been awarded a Zambian copper project.
By 0815 GMT Maranda shares had added 30 cents to 490 cents in volume of over 15,000 shares.
"It's up on the news that it was part of a consortium which got this award in Zambia. It's been quiet for so long and this news has woken it up," a share dealer said.
Maranda said earlier that the Metorex consortium, in which it holds a 30 percent stake, had been awarded Zambian Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd Chibuluma copper project.

It said the consortium would acquire an 85 percent shareholding in the Chibuluma project for an unspecified cash payment on September 30, further cobalt contribution linked payments and a financial commitment to commence development development of the project.
The Chibuluma project comprises an existing operating mine, Chibuluma West, currently producting some 9,500 tonnes of copper metal and 200 tonnes of cobalt a year.

The mine is one of the lower cost producers within ZCCM and has a proven reserve of a minimum of three years with the geological potential to continue operations beyond that, Maranda said in a statement.

The Metorex consortium, is jointly held by Maranda, Canadian development company Crew Development Corp, which holds 35 percent, South African investment bank Genbel Securities Ltd (Gensec) with 20 percent and unlisted junior mining company Metorex Ltd with 15 percent.
Gensec was last down 75 cents at 67.50 rand.
Maranda, a junior zinc-copper mine, debuted on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in May through a reverse listing into Rooiberg Tin Ltd.
